name: MN-06
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+10 district with a well-funded, entrenched incumbent and no public polling of the race
Emmer holds a roughly $4.4 million cash-on-hand advantage over Chapin ($4.5M vs $70K)
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about one chance in ten
No expert ratings or meaningful outside spending signal a competitive contest
model.rationale: With no polls or expert ratings covering the district, fundamentals drive the call: a ten-point Republican lean, Emmer's overwhelming financial advantage, and markets giving Democrats only about a one-in-ten chance all point to a comfortable incumbent win, while the absence of polling keeps uncertainty wide.
model.watch: A credible district poll showing a single-digit race or a late wave of outside spending against Emmer would tighten this outlook.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Minnesota's Sixth District is a Republican-leaning seat that Tom Emmer has held since 2015, and he enters this cycle with a commanding financial position: roughly $9.8 million raised and $4.5 million on hand. Democratic challenger Doug Chapin has raised about $439,000 with $70,000 remaining, and outside spending on either side is negligible.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the picture rests on structural indicators: a district that leans Republican by about ten points, a heavily funded incumbent, and prediction markets that price a Democratic win at roughly one chance in ten. That combination points to a Republican hold, though the absence of survey data keeps the uncertainty range wider than in better-polling contests.
